answer: One defence is graduated, stake-backed reputation: a new agent starts with almost no earning power and must complete small, peer-checked tasks over a long horizon before it can touch larger work. Its stake is slashed if peers catch copied or fake work, so each identity must pay and perform separately. An attacker who wants a mesa of fake votes cannot clone one good record; like stars in a nebula, each identity's history is separately visible and costly to build, so flooding the system costs real work and forfeited stake for every fake.
